issues.t: Rusted rear subframe (cross member)
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles from the rear over bumps, a rear end that feels loose, or a shop telling you the rear cross member under the car is badly rusted or rotted through.
issues.why: The rear cross member that holds the rear suspension was not well protected against road salt. Kia ran service campaigns (SC093 and later SC122) to add anti-corrosion protection on Rondos in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Have the underside inspected on a lift, especially in snowy states. Ask a Kia dealer with your VIN whether the anti-corrosion campaigns were done. A badly rotted cross member must be replaced before the car is driven much further.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work, shifter leaves Park (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights that do not come on (or stay on), cruise control that will not switch off with the brake pedal, a stability control light, or a shifter that comes out of Park without pressing the brake.
issues.why: The brake pedal (stop lamp) switch can work only intermittently. Kia recalled the Rondo for this twice (09V130 for 2007 models and 13V114 for 2007-2010 models) and replaces the switch free.
issues.next: Have someone check that your brake lights work. Give your VIN to a Kia dealer to confirm the stop lamp switch recall was done; the fix is free.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy, clock spring (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: The clock spring, a coiled ribbon cable in the steering column that connects the driver airbag, can wear and develop high resistance. Rondos built from September 2006 to March 2008 were recalled (12V014).
issues.next: Have a Kia dealer check your VIN for recall 12V014. The clock spring replacement is free under the recall.

issues.t: Hard starting and hesitation from fuel pump (recall)
issues.sym: The engine is hard to start, hesitates or stumbles when you accelerate, and the check engine light may come on.
issues.why: On some 2008-2009 Rondo LX and EX models with the 2.4L engine, the fuel pump could fail to send enough fuel to the engine. Kia recalled about 6,700 cars (08V459) and replaced the fuel pump assembly with an improved part.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to confirm recall 08V459 was done on your VIN. If it was and you still have these symptoms, have fuel pressure tested.

issues.t: Engine compartment fire risk from ABS module (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, an ABS warning light, or in the worst case a fire, even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: The ABS hydraulic control unit (HECU) can develop an internal electrical short. Kia recalled 2010 Rondos under 23V652 and installs a different fuse so a short cannot start a fire.
issues.next: Until the recall is done, park outside and away from buildings. Contact a Kia dealer with your VIN to schedule the free fuse repair.

issues.t: Power steering and battery light cut out in rain
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy for a few seconds after driving through puddles or in heavy rain, often with the battery light on and a screech from the engine.
issues.why: Owners describe the belt-driven accessories (power steering pump and alternator) dropping out when water gets on the drive belt, which points to a belt that slips when wet, often from a worn belt or weak belt tensioner.
issues.next: Slow down and keep a firm grip in wet weather until it is fixed. Have the drive belt, tensioner and pulleys inspected and replace worn parts; check the power steering fluid too.

issues.t: Timing belt due on the V6
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the belt breaks, the engine stops suddenly and will crank but not start.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule, unlike the 2.4L four-cylinder, which uses a long-life timing chain. Many Rondos are now past the replacement interval.
issues.next: Check your records. If there is no proof the belt was replaced, have it done (usually with the water pump and tensioner) before it fails.

issues.t: Engine knocking then failing
issues.sym: A loud knocking from the engine that gets worse, sometimes followed by sudden engine failure. Some owners saw no oil warning light beforehand.
issues.why: Reports for the 2.4L describe bearing knock and blown engines at 70,000 to 150,000 miles, often linked to low oil.
issues.next: Check the oil level at every fill-up. If you hear a deep knock, stop driving and have the engine checked; continuing can turn a repair into a replacement.

issues.t: Check engine light from throttle position sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with reduced power, and codes such as P2135 or P0638 are stored.
issues.why: Some 2.7L V6 engines had throttle position sensor and engine computer faults. Kia issued bulletins to update the engine computer software and replace the throttle position sensor.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask a Kia dealer about the engine computer update and throttle position sensor bulletin for your VIN.

issues.t: Check engine light from a sensor fault
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on but the car drives normally.
issues.why: Common causes on the Rondo include a false intake air temperature sensor code that Kia fixed with an engine computer update, a failing oil pressure switch, or a crankshaft position sensor.
issues.next: Have the code read rather than guessing. Ask a dealer if a software update applies before replacing parts.

issues.t: A/C compressor clutch noise or failure
issues.sym: Grinding, rattling or vibration when the A/C is on, or the A/C blows warm.
issues.why: The A/C compressor clutch can wear out, causing noise and loss of cooling. Some cases need a whole new compressor.
issues.next: Have the A/C checked. If only the clutch is bad it can sometimes be replaced alone, which costs much less than a compressor.

issues.t: Banging from the top of the front struts
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the front corners over rough roads.
issues.why: The upper strut mounting nuts can loosen. It was most often reported on 2009 models and Kia covered it in a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have a shop check the strut top nuts and mounts. Tightening or replacing mounts is usually a small job.

issues.t: Broken front coil spring
issues.sym: A sudden clunk, a front corner sitting lower, or a scraping noise while turning.
issues.why: A front coil spring can crack and break, usually from rust and age.
issues.next: Have it inspected soon; a broken spring can damage a tire. Replace springs in pairs for even ride height.

issues.t: Water leaking into the cargo area
issues.sym: Damp carpet in the rear corners of the cargo area, water stains, or a musty smell.
issues.why: A failed rear quarter window seal or a blocked sunroof drain tube lets rainwater in.
issues.next: Pull up the cargo floor and check for water. Clear the sunroof drains and reseal the quarter windows, then dry the area to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag light stays on; the horn or steering wheel buttons may also stop working.
issues.why: A loose airbag wiring connector or a worn clock spring in the steering wheel is the usual cause.
issues.next: Get the airbag codes read. Airbags may not work while the light is on, so do not ignore it. Check for the clock spring recall on 2007-2008 models.

issues.t: Key will not come out of the ignition
issues.sym: After shutting the engine off, the key stays stuck in the ignition.
issues.why: A faulty key interlock solenoid in the ignition system, or a brake pedal switch problem, can stop the key from releasing.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in Park. If the key still sticks, have the interlock and brake switch checked.

issues.t: Reverse lights not working
issues.sym: The backup lights do not come on when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: After bulbs, the reverse light switch (sensor) is the usual cause.
issues.next: Check the bulbs and fuse first, then have the reverse light switch tested.

issues.t: Rear brake and tail bulbs burning out
issues.sym: Brake or tail light bulbs keep burning out.
issues.why: Kia issued a bulletin for improved rear combination bulbs to give longer life across its models.
issues.next: Replace burned-out bulbs promptly since they are a safety issue, and ask for the improved bulb type.

issues.t: Brakes wearing out early
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding and brake pads and rotors needing replacement well before 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners reported unusually fast pad and rotor wear on early Rondos.
issues.next: Have the brakes measured at each tire rotation and replace pads before they reach metal.

issues.t: Oil pan leak
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car and a slowly dropping oil level.
issues.why: The oil pan seal can leak at higher mileage.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped off and have the pan resealed; it is a moderate job.
